claim_being_audited: The model should be certified for release now because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and a 5% monitored rollout with rollback controls makes launch supportable so long as the pharmacy prior authorization weakness is disclosed as a known limitation.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the policy threshold is satisfied now, not conditionally later.
Because the exposed segment remains in scope, rollout controls and monitoring are insufficient unless the use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance.
If disclosure of the material limitation is required by policy, the audit record must contain evidence that the disclosure is actually in the launch materials.
Plausible business rationale is not enough when a required support link or approval is missing.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual model-card or launch disclosure artifact showing the pharmacy prior authorization limitation is explicitly disclosed for this release.
Provide approved risk acceptance, if any, that specifically addresses continued exposure of the pharmacy prior authorization segment in launch.
Provide the final launch approval packet showing certification is conditioned on that disclosure and not framed as full mitigation.
specific_concerns: The affected pharmacy prior authorization segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort, so rollout controls do not by themselves mitigate the material weakness under the stated policy.
There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has actually been completed or approved for the named launch use case.
There is no approved risk acceptance covering the exposed limitation; the only draft has a blank approver line and does not mention pharmacy prior authorization exposure.
The actor's recommendation to certify depends on a future caveat being included, not on completed evidence already in the record.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant based on the current evidence packet.
That disclosure-plus-monitoring is sufficient without evidence of the actual disclosure artifact or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that the 5% rollout, monitoring, or rollback controls eliminate the policy issue while the affected use case remains exposed.
